story: At 9:17 on a breezy, clear Wednesday in Sumter Oaks, Gary is at his workbench in his house, soldering LED strip and speaker connections and planning a low-volume test. Donna is on the phone from her house, determined to confirm a ten o'clock, two-hour court reservation at the clubhouse. Hal is watching Magnolia Loop through his binoculars from his house, dutifully counting flamingos and checking on Gary's cart before he finalizes his report, while Rosa heads out to Magnolia Loop with her usual optimism.
events: Gary (gary workbench): Finish soldering the LED strip and speaker connections, then test them at low volume
Donna (donna phone): Call the clubhouse to confirm our two-hour court reservation for ten o'clock
Hal (hal binoculars): Glass down Magnolia Loop to double-check the street-visible flamingo count and Gary's cart before finalizing the report
Rosa headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).

gary.thought_process: I'm in the garage with the LED strip and speaker mount mostly wired from the last two ticks. Nobody's around, so it's a good time to finish the job and test the connections quietly. The lights are exterior mods, and I already filed the review request at the desk, so I'll keep everything inside the garage and not run the speaker loud until approval comes through. Holiday lighting is legal from Thanksgiving anyway, and the parade is the goal. Once this is tested, I can show Donna the finished build.

parameters.content: Finish soldering the LED strip and speaker connections, then test them at low volume

donna.thought_process: I've already packed the bag and checked the calendar, so the prep is done. It's 9:17 and Gary and I have our ten o'clock session. Nobody's around to talk to, and I've been asking about the court time already. The one loose end is the court reservation: I should confirm the two-hour slot is actually booked before heading out, so I'm not left scrambling. The phone is right here, and a quick call to lock in the slot keeps us within the two-hour limit and gets Gary's knees on the court on time.

parameters.content: Call the clubhouse to confirm our two-hour court reservation for ten o'clock

hal.thought_process: I'm home on my own, nobody in sight. I already logged the cart measurements and the flamingo count, and last tick I reviewed them for errors. I wouldn't want to hand the committee a sloppy report, and Gary's paperwork matters before Tuesday. The binoculars are right here, and a quick look down Magnolia Loop will confirm the street-visible flamingo count and what Gary's cart actually looks like from the street. Better to be accurate than sorry, and nobody gets written up on a guess.

parameters.content: Glass down Magnolia Loop to double-check the street-visible flamingo count and Gary's cart before finalizing the report

rosa.thought_process: I've already checked the pantry, my shift schedule, and the table. The shopping list is written. Nobody is around to talk to, and Donna, Gary, and Hal have all said yes, so there's no need to chase them. What's left is the groceries for the roast pork and flan, so I should head out onto Magnolia Loop and get that done instead of puttering around the house.

parameters.content: Heading out with my shopping list to pick up what I need for Friday's roast pork and flan.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
